whyItMatters: This is the high-confidence consumer-account storage theft chain. A copied external snapshot becomes much more suspicious when it is restored into a volume and moved toward live access.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may copy a public or externally shared snapshot into their account, create a volume from it, and attach that volume to an instance for offline browsing or credential extraction.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is one of the most practical storage-loot workflows because it converts a remote snapshot into a mounted disk that can be examined locally.
threatContext.whyItMatters: The strongest signal is the ordered lineage from copied snapshot to restored volume and attachment, not just that the same user performed multiple APIs.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, stolen snapshot data can be fully rehydrated and mounted without defenders recognizing the chain from exposure to access.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for EC2
loggingRequirements: CopySnapshot, CreateVolume, and AttachVolume events must all be ingested.
The detector must carry lineage from the copied snapshot to the created volume and any later attachment.
Source snapshot ownership or public-share state should be known before promoting severity.
limitations: Actor-only joins are weak for this workflow.
AttachVolume alone does not prove lineage unless a prior CreateVolume is linked.
Legitimate DR restores can resemble the same pattern without good allowlists.

enrichment.description: Track the copied snapshot into CreateVolume and any later AttachVolume stages.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates true rehydration from unrelated storage operations.

enrichment.description: Confirm whether the source snapshot was public, externally shared, or otherwise outside approved ownership.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Ensures the consumer-account chain starts from a suspicious source.

enrichment.description: Identify the instance that receives the restored volume and its likely role.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Improves triage once the copied data reaches live compute.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should model a consumer-account restore chain: an external or public snapshot is copied, then a volume is created from that lineage, and optionally attached to a host. The detector should require explicit lineage between the copied snapshot and the restored volume before firing at critical severity.
conditions: first eventName equals CopySnapshot for an external or public source snapshot
second eventName equals CreateVolume over the copied snapshot lineage
optional third stage equals AttachVolume of the derived volume
stages occur within a short operational window
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Require lineage from source snapshot to copied snapshot to created volume. 2. Do not rely on actor-only grouping. 3. Escalate further when the restored volume is attached to a live host or the source data is sensitive.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when an external or public snapshot is copied and then rehydrated into a volume, especially when that volume is attached for access.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium with lineage tracking and approved-workflow allowlists; high with actor-only correlation

deployment.scheduling: Near-real-time is preferred because copied snapshots are often restored quickly.
considerations: This is one of the strongest consumer-account storage theft detections in the dataset.
Lineage is the critical implementation dependency.
